tweets: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhānsī — born 19 November 1828. Her statues preserve a soldier's trick: sword in hand, reins gripped between her teeth, her son Damodar Rao bound to her back — so both arms stayed free for battle.

When the British annexed Jhānsī under the Doctrine of Lapse, she refused to cede her throne. In 1857 she led her army into revolt, falling in battle near Gwalior in 1858 — remembered as one of India's fiercest queens. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
